subject: Prompt cache hit assessment & next steps — pricing examples and target $/1M
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Chen <sophie.chen@quantapay.com>, Rick Morales <rick.morales@quantapay.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Prompt cache hit assessment & next steps — pricing examples and target $/1M

Hi Sophie / Rick — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and a short set of asks to keep momentum: 

Call summary (2 key takeaways)
- You expect ~2M prompt invocations/month initially with 15–25% weekly growth for Q3.
- Your primary objective is to get to an effective price that fits the internal budget band (~$X–$Y / month), and you wanted worked examples showing how cache hit assumptions move the effective $/1M tokens.

High-level caching assumptions I used (attached spreadsheet: redwood-cache-assumptions-v1.xlsx)
- Prefix / prompt-level caching (warm prefixes for common templates) — conservative hit-rate baseline: 35%
- Midcase: 55% hit, Upside: 75% hit (we modeled 35/55/75 for sensitivity)
- Baseline model cost (un-cached) = $40 per 1M tokens on the instance family we discussed (quantized variant).

Worked example (simple math to illustrate effective $/1M)
- Uncached: $40 / 1M tokens
- 35% hit: effective = 0.65 * $40 + 0.35 * $0 (cached) = $26 / 1M
- 55% hit: effective = 0.45 * $40 = $18 / 1M
- 75% hit: effective = 0.25 * $40 = $10 / 1M

Notes / caveats
- "Hit" above assumes full-response reuse for common prefixes (i.e., KV cache/prefix serves all non-personalized tokens). If prompts vary more, hit falls and effective price increases.
- We can model warm-start session caching to capture context carry that increases hit for multi-turn flows; I left that as a second tab in the workbook.

Asks / next steps
1) Can you confirm the 2M/month baseline (or send the true shape if it's more bursty)?
2) Share the proportion of prompts that are templated vs free-form (ballpark %) — that drives achievable hit.
3) We can run a 2-week pilot with instrumentation to measure real hit-rate before committing pricing. Would you prefer we scope that?

I attached the quick sensitivity workbook. I'll follow up with a detailed per-1M heatmap (40/60/80 hit grid) once you confirm volume shape. If useful, propose a 30-min follow-up Thursday morning PT — I can bring Monica to talk implementation specifics.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
(attachment stub: redwood-cache-assumptions-v1.xlsx)

On 2027-05-09 14:12, Jonas Weber wrote:
> Hi Sophie / Rick — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and a short set of asks to keep momentum: 

Thanks Jonas — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 
- 2M/month is a good baseline for Q3 (that’s ~65k/day on average) but traffic is highly diurnal and has bursts during batch runs — so we care about peak provisioning too.
- Templated vs free-form: roughly 60% templated (invoice templates, payment confirmations), 40% free-form (support chat, ad-hoc queries).
- Budget band: we are expecting to stay roughly in the $6k–$10k / month range while proving value; translated that into target effective price somewhere near $12–$20 / 1M tokens depending on adoption curves.

Can you and Monica send the 3-scenario (40/60/80 hit) worked example you mentioned plus a short note on how peak bursts affect expected instance sizing (and whether warm-session caching changes the peak compute needs)? That will help us route this through our procurement committee.

Appreciate it — Sophie
Sophie Chen
Head of Product, QuantaPay
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Sophie Chen <sophie.chen@quantapay.com>
Date: 2027-05-10T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Prompt cache hit assessment & next steps — pricing examples and target $/1M

Jonas / Aditya — I'll own the detailed econ modeling and the note on peak compute / sizing. Preliminary plan: 
- Build a 3x3 heatmap table: rows = hit rates (40/60/80), columns = monthly volumes (1M / 2M / 5M).
- Add a second table showing peak provisioning sensitivity (burst factor x1.5 / x2) to show compute delta and cost impact.
- Quick recommendation: if templated % >50% (which Sophie's at ~60%), warm-prefix caching + KV reuse typically moves you to the 60–75% band without additional engineering — we'll call that out.

I'll attach the modeled CSV and share a short slide with the procurement bullet points before EOD tomorrow. I'll also join the Thursday sync if scheduled.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Customer Success — Redwood Inference
